questions.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & -2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -6 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}9-\lambda  & -6 \\ -6 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (9-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-36 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda -4\lambda +36-36 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda  & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -13) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =13,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{13} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-4) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda ) & =0 \\ -\lambda (\lambda -1)(\lambda -4) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =4,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}|-4|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )[(5-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-4)]-16(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +16)-16(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda (4-\lambda )(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,4,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$  

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((1-\lambda )^{2}-1) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(1-2\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-1) & =0 \\ -\lambda (\lambda -1)(\lambda -2) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =2,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{2} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13 & 12 \\ 12 & 13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}13-\lambda  & 12 \\ 12 & 13-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (13-\lambda )(13-\lambda )-144 & =0 \\ 169-26\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-144 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-26\lambda +25 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda -25) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =25,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{25}=5 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$
